extracted.intended_audience: mathematics researchers and readers of the n-Category Café (category theory/algebra community)
extracted.subtask_description: A short blog post announcing and explaining the retraction of a published mathematics paper that claimed an impossible result (an associative 8-dimensional normed division algebra). It summarizes the reasons for retraction and the publisher's procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with established mathematical theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurwitz’s theorem says all 8-dimensional normed division algebras over the reals are nonassociative and isomorphic to the octonions; therefore there is no associative 8-dimensional normed division algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims claiming to find an object ruled out by a well-established theorem (here, an associative 8-dimensional normed division algebra) are treated as false; submitted results must be consistent with classical, well-established results or provide a convincing justification for overturning them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and integrity of mathematical argument (visible in title/abstract)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editors note 'The main error is visible not only in the title, but in the abstract which claims "... show that its eight-dimensional elements ... respect the norm relation ‖XY‖ = ‖X‖ ‖Y‖, thus forming an octonion-like but associative normed division algebra.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obvious contradictions or errors present in the title or abstract are grounds for concern about the integrity of the mathematics; such visible errors undermine confidence in the main result and can trigger editorial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial review and consultation process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editors 'have discussed this with the author, and sought additional review of these points of concern.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before retracting, editors should consult the author and seek additional expert review to assess the validity of concerns; this consultation is part of due process even if the outcome is a retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of publishing ethics policies and COPE guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editors state they were 'informed in our decision-making by our policy on publishing ethics and integrity and the COPE guidelines on retractions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to retract should be guided by the journal's publishing ethics policies and established guidelines such as COPE; these frameworks shape when and how retractions are issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of scholarly record with clear marking
rubrics_metrics.description: The retracted article 'will remain online to maintain the scholarly record, but it will be digitally watermarked on each page as "Retracted".'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When retracting, journals should keep the article accessible to preserve the record but clearly mark it (e.g., watermarking) so readers are informed that the results are not reliable.
